title: POC Weekly Sync - Quantization Experiments (INT8/FP8)
next_steps: Redwood to share updated perf spreadsheet (INT8/FP8 + KV cache) by 2025-07-10
Run end-to-end latency + tail-latency tests with INT8 + prefix caching (Liam) by 2025-07-11
Customer to provide canonical prompt set and 2-week traffic sample (Sofia) by 2025-07-09
Schedule deeper technical deep-dive on FP8 implications for per-layer accuracy with SE and Research (tentative week of 2025-07-14)
action_items: Maya Patel: Send perf/benchmark spreadsheet and brief note about quantization knobs (due 2025-07-10)
Liam Chen: Run INT8+KV cache latency run and upload logs to shared drive (due 2025-07-11)
Sofia Martinez: Share sample prompt set (30-50 prompts) and SLOs for quality (due 2025-07-09)
Rajiv Kapoor: Confirm allowed egress and VPN window for on-prem perf test (due 2025-07-12)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review INT8 vs FP8 quantization experiments. Redwood presented perf deltas and quality impact for the customer's prompt set; INT8 shows 2.2-2.8x token throughput improvements with small regression on a narrow subset of prompts. FP8 reduces quality loss but requires per-layer tuning. Agreed next steps: share detailed perf sheet, run additional latency tests with KV/prefix cache, customer to send canonical prompts and SLOs, schedule FP8 deep-dive.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Okay, good morning everyone, thanks for jumping on, uh this is our weekly POC sync, quick roll call.
[00:07] Sofia Martinez: Hi all, Sofia here.
[00:09] Rajiv Kapoor: Rajiv from infra.
[00:11] Julia Owens: Julia, CTO.
[00:13] Liam Chen: Liam, SE on the Redwood side.
[00:15] Maya Patel: Awesome. We put the agenda in the calendar: perf recap, quality review on customer prompts, then plan next runs.
[00:22] Sofia Martinez: Sounds good. We did run the smaller mix of prompts from last week, saw some... like a couple odd regressions but overall promising.
[00:30] Liam Chen: Cool. I can start with the perf numbers, I captured end-to-end and per-GPU token throughput. Note: these are using our INT8 path with the KV cache off vs on, and also an FP8 variant run where we enabled mixed FP8 on attention/ffn layers.
[00:45] Liam Chen: So baseline (fp16) throughput for the 8k seq model was about 120 tokens/sec per GPU. INT8 gave us an average of 280 tokens/sec per GPU (so ~2.3x) with CPU-side serialization unchanged. With prefix/KV cache enabled, E2E tail latency improved for repeated sessions, we saw median down 25% and p95 down 40% for warm sessions.
[01:10] Sofia Martinez: Wait, 280 tokens per second, is that with the same batching policy you ran last time?
[01:14] Liam Chen: Yes same batching (adaptive batching with 32ms target). We did verify with larger batch windows and saw slightly higher throughput but worse tail latency.
[01:21] Rajiv Kapoor: When you say KV cache enabled, is that the Redis-style external cache or the in-process prefix cache?
[01:25] Liam Chen: It's our in-process prefix KV cache for active sessions, we also tested an external caching setup in the cloud but perf gains were smaller due to network hops.
[01:33] Maya Patel: Important note: customer P95 SLO is 300ms end-to-end, right Sofia?
[01:36] Sofia Martinez: Correct, 300ms is our target for interactive product. Some of the INT8 runs hit that for median but p95 was borderline for cold sessions.
[01:45] Liam Chen: Right, cold sessions (no cache) have higher p95. With INT8 + prefix cache warm p95 was ~210ms, cold p95 about 420ms on the same config.
[01:54] Julia Owens: So FP8 helps with quality, I assume? What's the tradeoff on perf?
[01:58] Liam Chen: FP8 generally sits between fp16 and INT8. For these runs FP8 throughput was ~170 tokens/sec per GPU with much smaller quality regressions compared to INT8. So you trade a bit of throughput for higher fidelity. Also FP8 requires per-layer calibration in some models — not always plug-and-play.
[02:15] Sofia Martinez: We did see a few hallucinations increase on certain clinical prompts with INT8. Mostly the ones sensitive to numeric precision and tokenization edge cases.
[02:25] Liam Chen: Yup that's consistent with expected behavior; numeric-heavy prompts or long-range attention patterns can trigger small distribution shifts under INT8. We can try hybrid: INT8 for embeddings + attention but fp16/FP8 for ffn layers — it's a per-layer strategy.
[02:40] Rajiv Kapoor: Do you have an automated eval for those prompts? We want to reproduce the exact failure cases.
[02:45] Liam Chen: We do; we scoped a quality harness last week. Maya, I have the results linked in the drive: "quant-results-2025-07-07.xlsx" — there's a sheet with diff examples.
[02:56] Maya Patel: Yes link is in the meeting notes. We also annotated the prompts where BLEU-like and embedding-distance metrics diverged.
[03:05] Sofia Martinez: The problem is some of our prompts are short clinical queries that require precise token output — even small token shifts are unacceptable.
[03:14] Liam Chen: Makes sense. For those prompt classes we recommend either leaving fp16/FP8 or trying FP8-only for those layers and INT8 elsewhere. There's a per-prompt routing option in Redwood where you can route sensitive prompts to a higher-fidelity path.
[03:29] Julia Owens: That routing sounds useful but how does it affect cost predictability? We were hoping to get the cost benefits of INT8 across the board.
[03:34] Maya Patel: The routing is configurable — you can set rules to only route a small percentage of traffic to high-fidelity models. That keeps costs down while protecting critical prompts. We can show an expected cost delta in the perf sheet.
[03:45] Rajiv Kapoor: On infra: for the dedicated rig we are considering, what does FP8 mean for memory and kernel support? Any special drivers?
[03:53] Liam Chen: Mostly it's a model compilation/tuning step and the runtime needs kernel support which our Dedicated images include. For some GPU drivers you need the latest cuda/cuBLAS patches; our engineering notes list the driver versions. FP8 can reduce memory footprints slightly, but INT8 gives much bigger memory wins.
[04:10] Sofia Martinez: Can you summarize the quality delta numbers? Even rough is fine.
[04:14] Liam Chen: Sure. On our customer prompt set: average BLEU-like score vs baseline fp16: INT8 saw ~2-4% drop overall, but on the 7% of prompts labeled "sensitive" it was more like 8-12% drop. FP8 saw ~0.5-1.5% overall drop and 1-3% on sensitive prompts. These are approximate and depend on exact calibration.
[04:38] Sofia Martinez: 8-12% is concerning for us. Those are the 7% of prompts that represent critical clinical outputs.
[04:44] Maya Patel: Understood. So options we discussed: keep fp16 for the critical prompt set; try FP8 tuned for the whole model; or hybrid per-layer quantization. Each has different perf/cost tradeoffs.
[04:58] Rajiv Kapoor: For the pilot timeline, we were hoping to validate production config in two weeks. Is that feasible?
[05:02] Liam Chen: If you share canonical prompts and traffic pattern this week we can run the tuned INT8+FP8 hybrid and full FP8 runs next week and deliver a perf/quality report within 10 business days.
[05:14] Sofia Martinez: We can have the prompt set ready by Wednesday.
[05:16] Maya Patel: Great. We'll aim to have the perf spreadsheet out Friday.
[05:20] Julia Owens: A quick question on security implications: does FP8 change logging or token redaction behaviors?
[05:26] Liam Chen: No, quantization doesn't change logging. All logs and audit trails remain the same; model outputs are logged as before and you control retention/KMS.
[05:34] Rajiv Kapoor: For the end-to-end tests, we need to coordinate a maintenance window to allow higher load on the dedicated nodes. I'll propose a window next week.
[05:41] Maya Patel: Thanks Rajiv, put that in the shared calendar.
[05:44] Liam Chen: Quick note: we saw a specific regression on prompt ID 114 in the shared sheet where INT8 incorrectly reordered a short list — likely due to activation clipping. We can attempt per-layer PTQ calibration focused on the FFN there.
[05:57] Sofia Martinez: If you can fix that for the next run that would be ideal.
[05:59] Liam Chen: Will do.
[06:01] Maya Patel: Okay, are there any blockers from your side for the next experiments?
[06:05] Sofia Martinez: None besides the prompt set and confirming the egress/VPN window.
[06:10] Rajiv Kapoor: I'll confirm egress by Friday.
[06:12] Maya Patel: Great. For risk mitigation, we recommend a canary routing rule that sends 10% of traffic to INT8 initially and keeps 90% on fp16/FP8 until the regressions are addressed.
[06:24] Julia Owens: That is reasonable.
[06:26] Liam Chen: Also FYI we tested model fallback behavior — if the INT8 path fails post-deploy we'll auto-fallback to fp16 which avoids service disruption.
[06:36] Sofia Martinez: Good. One governance question: do you have audit logs per model version so we can correlate quality issues to rollouts?
[06:42] Maya Patel: Yes we have versioned deployments and audit logs including rollout timestamps and who triggered the change. We can provide examples.
[06:50] Rajiv Kapoor: Can we also get cost delta projections per 1M tokens for INT8 vs FP8 vs FP16?
[06:55] Maya Patel: We'll include that in the perf sheet — rough numbers plus estimated variance.
[07:00] Liam Chen: Another nuance: tokenization differences sometimes magnify under INT8 due to subtle floating point changes; we recommend normalizing tokenization and comparing logits distance not just tokens.
[07:12] Sofia Martinez: Noted.
[07:14] Maya Patel: Anything else on FP8 calibration?
[07:16] Liam Chen: We might need to do a per-layer grid search for FP8 scale factors; it can take a few iterations but usually 3-5 passes gets to acceptable accuracy.
[07:28] Sofia Martinez: That is fine, as long as we have a timeline.
[07:31] Maya Patel: We'll include estimated engineering hours in the next doc.
[07:35] Julia Owens: On business side, if the delta is acceptable we may expand pilot to additional models; otherwise we'll keep hybrid.
[07:43] Maya Patel: Noted.
[07:45] Liam Chen: Quick methodological note: we ran synthetic load and replayed 48 hours of traffic for tail latency; real traffic may show more variance but it's a good baseline.
[07:56] Rajiv Kapoor: For the replay tests we need sanitized PII — we will scrub before sharing.
[07:59] Sofia Martinez: We'll deliver scrubbed logs.
[08:02] Maya Patel: Perfect. Any other questions?
[08:05] Julia Owens: No, this was helpful.
[08:07] Maya Patel: Okay recap: Redwood shares perf spreadsheet by 2025-07-10, Liam runs INT8+KV cache latency tests and uploads logs by 2025-07-11, customer shares prompt set by 2025-07-09, Rajiv confirms egress by 2025-07-12. We'll schedule the FP8 deep-dive for week of 2025-07-14.
[08:27] Sofia Martinez: Thanks everyone.
[08:29] Maya Patel: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with links.
[08:31] Liam Chen: Bye all.
[08:33] Julia Owens: Bye.
[08:34] Rajiv Kapoor: Bye.

Note: Shared artifacts referenced: perf spreadsheet (drive link: drive.google.com/quant-results-2025-07-07), annotated diffs sheet, internal run logs (s3://redwood-poc/nimbus/quant-runs/2025-07-07).
